SUPERIOR COURT OF THE STATE OF WESTBROOK, COUNTY OF MARION

ANGELA J. WHITFIELD, individually and as
Administrator of the Estate of MARCUS WHITFIELD, deceased,
                Plaintiff,
        v.                              Case No. CV-2024-22107
WESTBROOK MEMORIAL HOSPITAL;
DR. KEVIN HOLBROOK, MD;
DR. ELAINE PETROV, MD;
                Defendants.

COMPLAINT FOR MEDICAL MALPRACTICE AND WRONGFUL DEATH

Plaintiff ANGELA J. WHITFIELD alleges:

PARTIES
1. Plaintiff is the surviving spouse of MARCUS WHITFIELD (DOB 02/18/1968; DOD 09/22/2024), and is the duly appointed Administrator of his Estate.
2. Defendant WESTBROOK MEMORIAL HOSPITAL ("WMH") is a 412-bed acute care hospital.
3. Defendant KEVIN HOLBROOK, MD is a board-certified Emergency Medicine physician who treated Decedent on 09/20/2024.
4. Defendant ELAINE PETROV, MD is a board-certified Internal Medicine hospitalist who admitted and treated Decedent from 09/20–09/22/2024.

FACTS
5. On 09/20/2024 at 04:14, Decedent presented to the WMH Emergency Department complaining of "the worst headache of my life," neck stiffness, photophobia, and a fever of 102.4°F. Vital signs on arrival: HR 124, BP 142/88, RR 22, SpO2 95%.
6. The triage nurse documented a chief complaint consistent with possible meningitis and assigned an ESI Level 2.
7. Defendant Holbrook examined Decedent at 05:48 — one hour and thirty-four minutes after triage — and ordered a CT head (without contrast), CBC, BMP, and blood cultures. He did NOT order a lumbar puncture and did NOT initiate empiric antibiotics within the 1-hour window recommended by the IDSA Practice Guideline for Bacterial Meningitis.
8. CT head was negative for mass effect, hemorrhage, or hydrocephalus.
9. At 08:22, after CT results returned negative, Defendant Holbrook documented a working diagnosis of "viral syndrome" and contacted Defendant Petrov for admission.
10. Decedent was admitted at 11:40 to the medical floor. Empiric antibiotics (ceftriaxone + vancomycin) were not ordered until 17:15 on 09/20/2024 — approximately 13 hours after presentation.
11. Lumbar puncture was performed at 22:08 on 09/20/2024 and confirmed bacterial meningitis (cloudy CSF, WBC 4,800, protein 312, glucose 18; Gram stain positive for Gram-negative diplococci).
12. Decedent rapidly decompensated overnight. He was transferred to the ICU at 04:02 on 09/21/2024 and died at 03:48 on 09/22/2024 from septic shock secondary to meningococcal meningitis.

STANDARD OF CARE
13. The standard of care for a patient presenting with classic meningitis symptoms is empiric IV antibiotics within ONE HOUR of suspicion, performed alongside (not after) diagnostic workup. (See Tunkel et al., IDSA Practice Guidelines, 2017.)
14. Each Defendant breached this standard. Defendant Holbrook delayed antibiotics by approximately 12 hours; Defendant Petrov failed to immediately escalate at admission.

CAUSATION
15. Expert opinion (see Affidavit of Dr. R. Park, attached) is that Decedent had >85% likelihood of survival had appropriate antibiotics been administered within the standard-of-care window.

CLAIMS
Count I — Medical Negligence (Holbrook)
Count II — Medical Negligence (Petrov)
Count III — Vicarious Liability (WMH, employer of both physicians)
Count IV — Wrongful Death (W.S.A. § 41-2-104)

WHEREFORE Plaintiff demands judgment in an amount to be proven at trial.

JURY TRIAL DEMANDED.

Dated: December 3, 2024
                                /s/ R. Suleiman, Esq.
